tex_content.label: gt.eq5.3
tex_content.html:
\begin{equation} \| x\| _{\B }\leq C\| L_tx\| _{\V } \end{equation} for every $x\in \B $ and $t\in [0,1]$, then $L_0$ is onto if and only if $L_1$ is onto.
Proof

Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0087 \sketch If $L_s$ is onto, (3) makes $L_s^{-1}$ well defined with norm at most $C$. Solving $L_tx=y$ is then the fixed-point problem

\[ x=L_s^{-1}y+(t-s)L_s^{-1}(L_0-L_1)x. \]

The right side is a contraction whenever $|t-s|<\{ C(\| L_0\| +\| L_1\| )\} ^{-1}$. Finitely many such intervals connect $0$ and $1$.

□
